item.title: Jockey Neale, 22, dies after fall during race
item.description: Izzy Neale turned professional in 2024 and rode 88 winners in her professional career [Getty Images] Jockey Izzy Neale has died after falling from her horse during a race at Warren Racecourse in Australia on Sunday. The 22-year-old was dislodged from her horse Marnoo and was airlifted to Dubbo hospital. Neale's family announced on Tuesday that she had passed away from her injuries. "It is with deep sadness and broken hearts that we announce the passing of our beloved Izzy, surrounded by her closest family and friends," a joint statement from the family and Racing NSW said. "Izzy rode horses before she could walk. Her love of horses was a lifelong passion that, more recently, had grown into a love of racing. "Through organ donation, Izzy will give others the chance of life, bringing some comfort to our family amid this devastating loss. "We are deeply grateful for the love, kindness and support shown to Izzy and our family by her friends, the racing community and everyone who has been by our side during this heartbreaking time." The rest of the Cotton Cup meeting was abandoned and Neale's horse Marnoo was euthanised after sustaining a serious leg injury in the accident. A second rider, Diego Montes de Oca, was injured in the same race. He suffered minor injuries to his foot and has since been discharged from hospital. Neale was an apprentice rider and rode 88 winners in her professional career. The Australian Turf club described Neale as a "talented young rider with a bright future". Trainer John Thompson, who Neale worked for, also paid tribute. "An absolute beacon of shining light. Always happy. Always smiling. Loved by everyone who met her," he said on X. "The world is poorer for the loss of a beautiful young lady. Heartbreaking." Neale's family thanked the public and the racing authorities in Australia for their support, as well as the medical staff who cared for her. "As we come to terms with our loss, we ask that our family's privacy be respected," they said. "Izzy was dearly loved and will forever be in our hearts." Latest horse racing results

item.description: Aaron Collins (right) has seven goals in the past three games for MK Dons and is the EFL's joint-top goalscorer [Getty Images] Wales have called up uncapped MK Dons striker Aaron Collins for this month's Nations League matches following Wrexham frontman Kieffer Moore's withdrawal due to injury. Moore, 34, left the field during Wrexham's 1-1 Championship draw with Wolves on Saturday. Wales have not specified what kind of injury the 57-cap forward has sustained. He is replaced in the Wales squad by Collins, who has scored 17 goals in 16 games across all competitions for League One side Dons this season, including four goals in a game against Doncaster last month. The 29-year-old former Newport County player joins Craig Bellamy's squad for concluding Group A4 games in Norway and at home to Portugal. Newport-born Collins has played for 10 different - mainly lower league - clubs since leaving Rodney Parade for Wolverhampton Wanderers in 2016. Wales, who are looking to preserve their place in the Nations League's top tier, face Norway in Oslo on Saturday before finishing their campaign at home against Portugal next Tuesday. Wales are third in Group A4, with their only win from four matches so far coming against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway in Cardiff last month. Bellamy is without midfielder Jordan James but has influential Leeds pair Harry Wilson and Joe Rodon back, along with Cardiff playmaker Rubin Colwill. Bellamy's side could still finish in second, third or fourth place. A top-two spot would take Wales to the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2027. Finishing third would mean a relegation play-off against a League B team in March, while finishing bottom of the group would result in either a relegation play-off or direct relegation, depending on the ranking with other League A groups. item.title: Rudi Völler suggests Thomas Müller could follow him into DFB role
item.description: Rudi Völler suggests Thomas Müller could follow him into DFB role Rudi Völler has named former Bayern Munich star Thomas Müller as a potential successor to him as sporting director of the German Football Association (DFB). The 66-year-old, whose current deal expires in 2028, said on the “Kerners 11” podcast: “At some point, my time will finally come to an end. And if the DFB – whether [DFB president] Bernd Neuendorf, [DFB vice-president] Aki Watzke or managing director Per Mertesacker – feels that someone else should be brought in, I think that would be a good idea.” Völler added that he's "absolutely convinced" Müller would be suitable for the role. "Thomas could certainly do it, just like others could. Whether in my position or another one. They would just have to want it – that's the basis," he said. Since leaving Bayern Munich at the end of the 2024/25 season, 36-year-old Müller has been playing for Vancouver Whitecaps in Major League Soccer, where his contract runs until the summer of 2027.

item.title: Liverpool leading the race to sign Bundesliga defender
item.description: Liverpool leading the race to sign Bundesliga defender Liverpool Lead Castello Lukeba Race as Defensive Planning Accelerates Liverpool’s transfer window continues to move on several fronts, and one of the more persuasive developments concerns Castello Lukeba. According to Football FanCast, the Merseyside club are currently the most interested Premier League side in signing the RB Leipzig centre-back, with Arsenal and Manchester United also in the picture. What gives this report added weight is the suggestion that the player’s camp have made clear his preference for a move to the Premier League. That does not make a deal imminent, and it certainly does not remove the complexity of negotiating with Leipzig, but it does shape the landscape. When a player’s representatives begin informing interested clubs of a desired destination, recruitment departments tend to sharpen their focus quickly. Photo: IMAGO Castello Lukeba emerges in Liverpool transfer plans Liverpool have already committed huge money to squad building, yet the sense remains that defensive work is still ongoing. That is understandable. Squad planning rarely stops at headline spending totals, particularly when contract timelines and age profiles begin to influence medium-term decisions. At centre-back, there is an obvious need to think ahead. Virgil van Dijk remains a towering presence, but any elite club must prepare for succession before necessity becomes urgency. Joe Gomez’s situation also forms part of that wider conversation, while depth across the back line has been examined closely as Andoni Iraola shapes the next phase of his squad. Lukeba, at 23, fits the profile Liverpool often pursue when they believe a player can grow into a leading role. He is young, already experienced at a high level, and naturally left-footed, an attribute that can materially influence build-up structure and balance in a back line. Those qualities alone help explain why multiple English clubs have tracked him. RB Leipzig defender suits Andoni Iraola system The tactical appeal is clear. Liverpool’s defensive unit needs players comfortable defending space, aggressive in duels and composed enough to progress possession under pressure. Lukeba has long been regarded as a defender with those traits, which is why admiration around Europe has endured. Another point in this case is contractual. The original report indicates that Lukeba has a release clause, which can simplify parts of a transfer if a buying club decide conditions are favourable. A clause does not guarantee completion, but it can offer certainty over the level required to open the door. That matters in a market where Liverpool are balancing ambition with discipline. item.title: ‘Scariest part’: Dwyane Wade says Steph Curry’s ‘best skill’ is not actually his shooting
item.description: Photo by Tom Pennington/Getty Images Steph Curry is one of the best players in the world. The Golden State Warriors superstar is still playing at an elite level at the age of 38, and he is continuing to break all sorts of records. Most people would say that Curry’s best skill is his shooting from three-point range, but Dwyane Wade thinks it’s actually something else. Dwyane Wade says Steph Curry’s cardio is actually his best skill Curry is widely regarded as the greatest shooter in basketball history. The way he shoots and the areas he occupies completely changed how defences guard the perimeter, and he’s still impossible to stop at times. That is why many would call shooting Curry’s best skill, but Wade believes it’s his cardio and off-ball movement. He said on his podcast : “I think his best skill is his cardiovascular. Steph doesn’t look like he ever gets tired. He’s always moving. “The scariest part about guarding Steph Curry is when he gives the ball up. That’s saying a lot about a guy who was dynamic with the ball in his hand. But when Steph Curry gives that ball up, watch out! “That’s what makes them (Warriors) great is when Steph gives that ball up and now he is moving, and everybody is doing their job. They’re setting screens in. They’re ducking in. “You had guys that wanted to be isolation guys. They don’t do a lot of isolation basketball in Golden State. It’s movement. It’s body movement. It’s ball movement. It’s making sure that the defence is not comfortable in their positions.” Wade finished off by saying that Curry’s mere presence on the court is an assist to everyone else because of his movement with and without the ball. “Forget hockey assist. Steph on the floor is an assist for everybody because of his body movement and the ball movement that comes with that.” We’d still attribute Curry’s best skill to shooting, but Wade’s assessment makes complete sense. The way the 38-year-old moves with and without the ball makes him so difficult to guard. All it takes is one mistake, and that opens the door for him to shoot – and he almost always scores. That is why Curry is among the greatest players of all time. item.title: What LA Rams sources were saying about Terrance Ferguson just before his hamstring injury
item.description: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images Terrance Ferguson has played just three games so far this season for the Los Angeles Rams, so here’s the latest from sources within the camp. The Los Angeles Rams are 5-4 through nine games this season, with their most recent game a 13-20 loss to the Commanders just as they were gaining momentum. It’s clear they are missing sophomore tight end Terrance Ferguson, who has missed six games due to a variety of issues. Just as he was coming back from an ankle issue, Ferguson did his hamstring, and it threw a spanner in the works for the Rams. LA Rams sources on Terrance Ferguson The Rams intended to slowly bring Ferguson along after he played 14 games last season and started only three of those. The three games he did play this season were all starts, so the Rams clearly have a bigger role for him this season, even though he hasn’t been able to fulfil it. The Rams could certainly use his explosiveness, but repeated injuries to the lower half of his body will eventually take a toll on his output. Meanwhile, his hamstring injury set him back further, and according to Graziano, speaking on ESPN, it is a huge blow because Ferguson figured to be a huge part of their plans this season. He said: “I was talking to Rams people on Friday, just doing prep for the game, and a couple of people were talking about how with Davante out, it’s just Puka. How do you combat that? “They said, “Well, we’re like the 13 personnel team.” Obviously, they’ve got the tight ends. They were saying having Terrance Ferguson back this week is massive. He’s a huge part of the game plan. “This was Friday at 5 p.m. Eastern. Ten minutes after those phone calls were over, I got the updated Rams injury report. Terrance Ferguson had pulled his hamstring in practice. He’s not going to play. So they had a Terrance Ferguson game plan.” Knowing what we know now, it’s not very surprising that the Rams lost to the Commanders, since a huge part of their plans pulled out of the game on short notice before the game. Now the wait begins on his latest injury, hoping that the layoff is not huge, but he looks like a certainty to miss their next game against the Cardinals. At least they will know they are planning without him this time! item.title: No Suspension for Tom Wilson after Hit on Sandis Vilmanis. That’s Wrong
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Washington Capitals play in Ottawa tonight and Tom Wilson will be in the lineup as if his cheap hit on Florida rookie Sandis Vilmanis never happened. Perhaps we did not see it as well as the NHL’s Department of Player Safety did. Wilson, long one of the NHL’s biggest cheap-shot artists, will not face any sort of supplemental discipline for boarding Vilmanis in the first period of Washington’s 4-3 win over the Panthers on Saturday afternoon. The punishment, we guess, of being kicked out of the game was plenty enough. Wilson has probably learned his lesson. After being suspended six other times, we seriously doubt it. And, based on the language Wilson used on the game officials who tossed him Saturday as he took his sweet time getting to the Washington room, he thought that punishment was too harsh. Really, it was not even close to being enough. Florida coach Paul Maurice was asked about the hit and deferred comment, saying he would “save that for the Department of Player Safety.’’ ”That’s their job,’’ Maurice said. Well, it was not done. Wilson knew full well that Vilmanis was in a vulnerable position along the boards. Vilmanis worked the puck up the ice and Wilson bulldozed him from behind, planting the Florida forward face-first into the dasher boards. There was no doubt it was a boarding call — the puck left Vilmanis’ stick moments before impact — and Wilson had full view of Vilmanis’ number, name plate, and even the small Panthers’ logo on the back of his white helmet. Ever see a young hockey player wearing a jersey to a game and notice the big red stop sign stitched onto the back? It there as a reminder to players not to hit another player in the back. When you see the numbers, stop. Perhaps teams playing the Capitals from now on should put those stop signs on the back of their sweaters. Probably would not help anyway. Vilmanis, 22, missed Sunday’s game in Boston and will likely be out tonight in Columbus as well. Maurice said the Panthers will not know the severity of Vilmanis’ injury until team doctors in Florida get to take a look at him. It is possible Vilmanis skipped the team charter and returned to town. Vilmanis is expected to be fine and he will return to the Florida lineup in time. That is not the point. Wilson has been a dangerous and, based on his 30-plus goals the past two seasons, very talented forward in this league who is now making high-end money. He does not need to keep playing this way to “keep his edge” nor to keep his job. Again, he just needs to do better. Perhaps some day. item.description: Motorsport photo The FIA has announced its final Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) results for the 2026 Formula 1 season, with no changes granted for any of the power unit manufacturers. From this season, the FIA installed a mechanism in the F1 regulations which allowed power unit manufacturers the ability to make updates, if they fell behind the leading engine, in the form of tokens permitted under a performance scale. After the first period in 2026, which ran from the Australian Grand Prix to the Canadian GP, it was announced that Red Bull Ford Powertrains emerged as the benchmark, while Mercedes ’ internal combustion engine trails by between 2-4%, which gave the German manufacturer to one additional upgrade this year and one more next season. Ferrari , Audi and Honda fell into the category of being more than 4% behind on ICE power, which grants them two upgrades during the current campaign and two more in 2027. Red Bull Ford Powertrains asked for a review of the ADUO analysis, which delayed the official publication of the first results, as it disputed the results and being considered the manufacturer with the strongest engine. As agreed before the start of the season by the teams, the FIA only measures the internal combustion engine, but once a manufacturer qualifies for ADUO, it is also allowed to modify electrical components such as the battery and MGU-K. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing So while Red Bull’s rivals have been able to install power unit upgrades across this season, the Milton Keynes-based effort has effectively faced an engine freeze. In the third and final FIA analysis of ADUO – which took engine data from the Dutch GP up to and including the US GP – there has been no change and therefore no manufacturer will gain or lose its current concessions. There was also no change in the second ADUO period over the summer. “For the third period, the relative performance gaps to the leading ICE evolved, but these changes did not result in any additional homologations being granted to the Power Unit Manufacturers,” an FIA report stated. Given the dispute over how ADUO is measured, the FIA is open to changes in the system in the future, subject to approval from the power unit manufacturers, while FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis is confident the concept is working as desired. “The FIA has undertaken extensive analysis as part of the review of ADUO this year. Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached,” Tombazis said. item.description: Galatasaray-vs-Juventus-Champions-League-2025-26-KO-play-offs-1s - AFP Kenan Yildiz is nearing his highly anticipated return for Juventus after missing several months of action due to injury. The talented forward recently provided a positive update on his recovery, revealing his target date to finally step back onto the pitch this December. Juventus handed major injury boost Yildiz is finally closing in on a return to action for Juventus following a frustrating spell on the sidelines. The 21-year-old has been unavailable due to injury since August , dealing a significant blow to the Italian club. According to Tuttosport , the talented forward will soon resume his individual training programme at the Continassa base. He will then gradually increase his physical workload as he builds up his crucial match fitness. Yildiz will not be ready to feature immediately after the current international break. Juventus are carefully managing his recovery process to ensure he returns in optimal physical condition. Yildiz reveals his comeback timeline The attacker recently attended a ceremony in Bologna on Monday to collect the Bulgarelli Number 8 award. During the event, he provided a highly positive update regarding his ongoing rehabilitation. Yildiz confirmed directly to those in attendance that he expects to be back "in December". The Juventus number 10 expressed his deep desire to get back onto the pitch and contribute alongside his team-mates. "I feel good and I hope to be playing again soon," Yildiz explained when discussing his fitness. "I miss Juventus so much. I miss the feeling of playing football." Coping without the number ten Juventus have been forced to navigate the early months of the campaign without their creative focal point. Despite the lengthy and frustrating absence, Luciano Spalletti has notably refused to use the injury as an excuse. The club and medical staff have now plotted a clear timeline for his gradual reintroduction. A return against Monza on Monday, 14 December at the Allianz Stadium is currently viewed as the most realistic target. Yildiz remains eager to accelerate that process if his body allows it over the next fortnight. The coaching staff will monitor his daily progress closely as he ramps up his training workload. Crucial fixtures await the forward While the Monza fixture remains the primary objective, Juventus are quietly hoping Yildiz could make the matchday squad even sooner. His early availability would provide a timely lift for the busy winter schedule. An accelerated recovery could see him feature in the domestic home game against Udinese on 6 December. Alternatively, he might travel for the Europa League clash against Hapoel Be’er Sheva in Bucharest just four days later. A December return will ultimately provide a massive mid-season boost for Juventus. Yildiz will now focus entirely on completing his individual work at Continassa to make that comeback a reality.

item.description: Barcelona defender Cubarsi named 2026 Golden Boy winner Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsí has won the 2026 Golden Boy award, given to the best Under-21 men’s player in the world. The 19-year-old succeeds Paris Saint-Germain forward Désiré Doué and becomes the fourth Barcelona player to win the prize in the last six years. Cubarsí follows in the footsteps of team-mates Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal, who have all previously claimed the award. He is also the first defender to win the Golden Boy since Matthijs de Ligt, then of Ajax, was named the winner in 2018. The award was established by Italian sports newspaper Tuttosport in 2003 and has previously been won by some of the biggest names in world football. Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Rajasthan Royals have also been discussing a Romario Shepherd-for-Sam Curran swap, which is a like-for-like trade. Set against the three seasons that preceded it, there is clearly a reverse trend. Since 2023, squads have been built around specialists because of the Impact Player rule, which allowed teams to add an extra player in between matches. Sachin Tendulkar urged the board to drop it. Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Hardik Pandya, Axar Patel and Shubman Gill have all raised the same objection: that the rule devalues genuine all-rounders by letting teams field a specialist for every job. The board's own behaviour has been contradictory. In late September 2024, it confirmed the Impact Player would run through the 2025-2027 cycle. item.description: Mancini’s former teammate reveals: ‘He was unbearable at first, I locked him in a room’ Italy coach Roberto Mancini was “unbearable” when they first played together, according to Michele Serena, who says he once locked the Sampdoria star in a room until they sorted out their differences. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, via CalcioMercato , the former full-back looked back on a career that took him from Venezia to Juventus, Sampdoria, Fiorentina, Atlético Madrid, Parma and finally Inter, the club he supported as a boy. He joined Sampdoria from Juventus as part of the deal that took Gianluca Vialli to Turin. “Roberto Mancini? Very good, but unbearable,” Serena said. “I argued with him in my first year, and Mantovani fined him and took my side. Vierchowod told me to apologise to Mancini, so after one training session I locked him in a small room with me until we finally sorted things out. After that, we built a good relationship, and we still speak today.” BURSA, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 28: Roberto Mancini, Head Coach of Italy, looks on before the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Türkiye and Italy at Atatürk Spor Kompleksi Matli Stadyumu on September 28, 2026 in Bursa, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images) Serena on Mancini, Mihajlović and Batistuta Sinisa Mihajlović was another Sampdoria teammate, and he used to make Serena go in goal. “After training, Mihajlović would put me in goal and take free-kicks. It would finish 20-0 or 20-1 to him.” At Fiorentina, Serena played alongside Gabriel Batistuta and Rui Costa. “Bati was the most complete No 9 I’ve ever seen. With Rui, we always wondered how he could smoke so many cigarettes and then run like that on the pitch. “Edmundo? I’ll never forgive him for not coming back from the Rio Carnival. We had Batistuta out, and we were fighting for the Scudetto.” 12 Sep 1998: Gabriel Batistuta of Fiorentina celebrates during the Serie A match against Empoli at the Stadio Communale in Florence, Italy. Mandatory Credit: Allsport UK /Allsport Serena finished his career at Inter in 2003, but he’s still haunted by 5 May 2002. On the final day of that season, Héctor Cúper’s side lost 4-2 at Lazio, and Juventus took the title. “I wanted to retire by winning the Scudetto with Inter, the team I’ve supported since I was a child. Instead, on that 5 May, I don’t know what happened… It’s a wound that’s still open, and it still hurts too much today. “I was supposed to play that day instead of Gresko. I’d done everything to recover from an injury, but Cúper changed his mind at the last minute. I confronted him about it, because not playing that day really hurt me.”

item.description: “I can’t believe this is happening”, says Brazil newcomer Allan New call-up Allan gave his first press conference with the Brazilian national team on Tuesday (10) and emphasized how hard it still is to believe he has been called up to the Seleção. In Singapore for friendlies against Japan and the hosts, the forward explained that his first few days with the team still do not feel real. “I'm definitely very emotional. Until very recently, this seemed so far away,” he admitted. Allan during his first press conference with the Brazilian national team in Singapore Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF This is his first opportunity with the senior national team. At youth level, he represented the Under-15s while playing for Figueirense. He attended a training camp at Granja Comary in July 2018 and another in Chile in August 2019, when Brazil beat the hosts in two friendlies: 5–0 and 2–1. Despite his nerves, he relies on his family's faith in him to keep his emotions in check and maintain the performances that earned him his call-up. “It's very difficult to come here and see players like Raphinha, Vini Jr. and even Endrick. Being here for the first time... My father tells me I'm capable, that if I'm here, I have talent too. On the pitch, I forget everything and focus fully on my performance,” he stressed. Before that, he made his name at Palmeiras, where he played almost a hundred matches and established himself as yet another outstanding talent to emerge from the club. The Florianópolis native, from the state of Santa Catarina, is one of 25 players called up for the friendlies against Japan and Singapore. item.description: Coutinho 2.0? Liverpool make their move for Brazilian starlet after recent contract decision Almost 14 years on from signing Philippe Coutinho , Liverpool are reportedly making moves to potentially sign another Brazilian playmaker who’s been attracting some high-profile European interest. The Reds’ former number 10 spent five years at Anfield, during which time he scored 54 goals in 201 appearances and was a hugely influential figure on the pitch, frequently conjuring up moments of majesty. He was sold in January 2018 and wasn’t around for the peak years of the Jurgen Klopp reign, although there’s an up-and-coming talent from Brazil who LFC will be hoping can become synonymous with a successful era under Andoni Iraola. Liverpool enquire about Erick Bele According to Sport Witness , Liverpool have made official enquiries with Palmeiras about 19-year-old attacking midfielder Erick Bele, with the Brazilian club prepared to start negotiations at €30m (£25m). Paris Saint-Germain have also been in contact regarding the teenager, who signed a contract extension to 2031 with his current employers last week. The youngster stood out during a recent training camp for Brazil under-20s in which he provided three assists across wins over Denmark, United States and Mexico. Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Could Bele go on to become Coutinho 2.0 at Liverpool? Bele has an impressive record at youth level for Palmeiras, with 20 goals in 45 games for their under-20 side, although his development is being managed carefully as he’s made just seven senior appearances so far ( Transfermarkt ). He plays mostly as a number 10 but can also be deployed on the right flank, similar to Harvey Elliott, and it attests to how highly his club value him that they’ve rewarded him with such a lengthy new contract. An analysis from Future Ballers cites finishing, pace, dribbling, technique, heading, off-the-ball movement and creativity among his strongest attributes, marking him out as a well-rounded young talent who also boasts plenty of physical strength. Even if Liverpool were to sign Bele in 2027, realistically he wouldn’t be challenging for a first-team place straight away, given his inexperience at senior level and the presence of Florian Wirtz in the Reds’ XI. A loan move or two to clubs in mainland Europe would likely be arranged in order to enhance his development, but we can certainly see why Anfield chiefs have enquired about an exciting prospect who, in time, could have strong echoes of Coutinho.

item.description: The future of Dunwoody (GA) High School football is being built by more than just the players on the field. It's being built by hundreds of community members who have come together to give the Wildcats something they've never had before: a stadium of its own. Fueled by a donation from Dunwoody alum and television host Ryan Seacrest and a community-wide fundraising effort, Seacrest Stadium is officially set to break ground the week of Nov. 23, following county approval on Nov. 9. And when it opens next fall, the whole community will be able to call it their own. “I think we’re all kind of part owners of this,” said Steve Fortenberry, former teacher and president of the Dunwoody High School Community Association. “I think you’re really going to see that it wasn’t just the county building this and we show up. This is Dunwoody’s stadium. We are kind of the Green Bay Packers of the high schools.” The project has been years in the making, but it took a collective effort from the community to turn the vision into a reality. It started with a donation of more than $1 million from Seacrest, who played defensive back for the Wildcats before graduating in 1993. “For us, it’s about so much more than a field,” Seacrest said in a statement provided to USA TODAY Sports. “It’s about creating a place where kids can dream big, chase those dreams and have the support of their families every step of the way. “To be part of something that celebrates both the dreams and the people who help make them possible is what makes this moment so special.” Seacrest’s donation made what once seemed like an unrealistic goal attainable, giving the community a foundation to launch its own fundraising effort: the “Bring It Home Dunwoody” campaign. In October, the school officially reached its goal of raising an additional $1.5 million. The money, raised by nearly 800 community members, will go towards 2,000 new stadium seats, a press box, restrooms, concessions and other stadium amenities. “There is something special about our community that you have to be a part of it to really understand how special Wildcat Pride is and what Dunwoody is all about," said Tom Bass, principal of Dunwoody High School. item.description: Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images Yaxel Lendeborg is never too far away from the headlines when the Golden State Warriors are playing. Steph Curry and Brandin Podziemski scored 25 points each, while Lendeborg added 23 of his own in a largely one-sided fixture. The Pelicans, understandably, got more and more frustrated as the game went on, and emotions got the better of Derik Queen in the fourth quarter. When Graham Ike got a rebound, Queen fouled him and then shoved him away for no reason. That’s when Lendeborg stepped in with a small push of his own and a few words on top of it. Speaking about the incident in his press conference, the rookie claimed that he was just trying to send a message to the Pelicans centre to not mess with his teammates. He said, as per KNBR : “He just pushed Graham. That was kind of crazy. So I just said a couple of cuss words in a ‘don’t do that’ kind of way. “And then he came up on me, and I tried to do a little foul. It wasn’t as hard as I intended for it to be but, just trying to send a message – don’t mess with the guys!” Both Queen and Lendeborg were given technical fouls for their actions, and that was the end of that. The Warriors have now extended their winning streak to eight games, and they are really looking like a force to be reckoned with. Lendeborg, despite actions like the above, is playing his part on the court, and he is likely to win the Rookie of the Year award if he continues performing at the same level.
